standing_findings.severity: latent defect in the revert path
standing_findings.scope: NOT specific to this run - applies to any future run of this shape
standing_findings.shape_that_triggers_it: A single file written more than once in one run (e.g. an initial packet plus one or more review-driven corrections), where the file is UNTRACKED in git.
standing_findings.what_happens: write-provenance --before takes a backup per write. On the 2nd and later writes the 'pre-write' state is already the run's own intermediate output, so backups/ ends up holding the INTERMEDIATE content, not the pre-run original. The earliest record's sha_before still names the true original, but no artifact on disk contains it.
standing_findings.consequence: For a TRACKED file this is harmless: git holds the original and is the authoritative restore source. For an UNTRACKED file there is no git copy and the backup is wrong, so /mmo:revert has NO correct restore source at all and would 'restore' the file to a half-corrected state while reporting success.
standing_findings.observed_here: This run wrote apps/docs/core/functional/plan-and-execute-tasks.mdx twice (tp_docs_002 then tp_docs_003). backups/ holds sha256:831e57... (the intermediate, containing the since-corrected phrase 'selected values'), while the true original is sha256:0eb427... This run was safe ONLY because the file is tracked_in_git: true.
standing_findings.suggested_fix: write-provenance --before should skip taking a backup when a record for that path already exists in this run (first-write-wins), or write backups to per-write filenames and have revert select the earliest.
standing_findings.status: open - filed as a standing finding, not remediated by this run
